reason: The cited evidence supports that laser cladding can improve TC4 surface properties and that HEAs have high hardness/wear resistance, but it provides no specific prior evidence for HEA coatings on TC4, the claimed 50–70% hardness increase, or the preservation of substrate properties. The cited studies involve different coating materials (e.g., TiAl-based composites), not HEAs.
premises: Laser cladding can produce dense, metallurgically bonded coatings on TC4 with refined microstructures.
High-entropy alloys (HEAs) possess high hardness and wear resistance.
Applying a HEA coating via laser cladding will form hard phases and a refined structure that increases hardness and reduces wear.
The HEA coating will not compromise the beneficial properties of the TC4 substrate (e.g., low density, corrosion resistance).
A hardness increase of 50–70% and a measurable decrease in wear rate are expected based on similar literature reports.
